sections.content:
Big change! Clicking the g tile at (1,3) (19,30):
- The selected dot at (1,1) disappeared (N→w, ring G→W).
- The dot at (1,2) also disappeared (N→w).
- The g tile at (1,3) became a green dot (N).
So, the two dots at (1,1) and (1,2) merged into the tile at (1,3)?! The green dots at (1,1) and (1,2) moved/vanished, and the dot at (1,3) appeared.
Wait, let me double-check: before this click, the dots were at (1,1) [selected], (1,2), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5). After: the dots are at (1,3)?? and (1,4), (2,5), (4,5). Looking at the image: the green dots are now at (1,2)... hmm, in the image the dots are at columns 2 and 3 of row 1 (i.e., grid (1,2) and (1,3))? Let me check the image: the dots are at roughly x=115 and x=137, which is columns 23-26 and 29-32 → grid (1,2) and (1,3). Hmm, wait, the diff says:
- (18,24),(18,25) N→w: the top edge of dot (1,2) disappeared.
- (19,23..26) N→w: dot (1,2) disappeared.
- (18,30),(18,31) g→N; (19,29..32) g/w→N; (20,29..32) g→N; (21,30),(21,31) g→N: a complete 4x4 dot appeared at (1,3).
So now the dots are at: (1,3), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5). Four dots.
So, clicking the highlighted g tile "merged" the selected dot (1,1) and the adjacent dot (1,2) into (1,3)?? That's strange. Or: the selected dot (1,1) moved to (1,3), and the dot at (1,2) was... absorbed?
Hmm, wait. Maybe the mechanic is: click a dot to select it (ring + the tile two cells away is highlighted?). Then click the highlighted tile to move the dot there, and the dot passes through/absorbs the dot at (1,2)?
Or: the g tile at (1,3) was a "merge target": the dots at (1,1) and (1,2) combine into one at (1,3)?
Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the mechanic is "2048-style merging": the selected dot + the adjacent dot merge into the next cell? The dot at (1,1) was selected, the dot at (1,2) is adjacent, and the merge result appeared at (1,3) (the next cell in the direction of the adjacent dot). This is exactly like 2048: when you move right, adjacent same-value tiles merge into the next position.
But wait, in 2048 the merge happens when you press the arrow key. Here, clicking the g tile triggered it. Hmm, but maybe the g tile at (1,3) was a "preview" of the merge result: when I selected the dot at (1,1), the game computed that pressing RIGHT would cause (1,1) and (1,2) to merge into (1,3), and highlighted (1,3) as g. Then clicking that tile executed the merge?
Or more simply: clicking a tile adjacent to the selected dot moves the selected dot there, and... no, (1,3) is not adjacent to (1,1).
Let me think about 2048 on this L-shaped board: the tiles are the "cells" of the grid, and the green dots are the "numbers" (all the same value?). Goal: merge all the dots into one? If all the dots are the same value, merging two makes one (like a "same-value" merge). The goal might be to reduce the 5 dots to 1.
But how does the arrow key fit in? In 2048, arrow keys move all the tiles in that direction. Earlier, when I pressed RIGHT without a selection, nothing happened... but wait, in 2048, pressing RIGHT should move the dots to the right! The dots at (1,1), (1,2) should merge into (1,3)... but nothing happened. Hmm, unless the arrow key only moves the selected dot.
Actually wait — maybe the arrow key does move the selected dot, but the first RIGHT (before selection) had no selection so nothing happened. After selection, I pressed RIGHT and only the top bar changed... that contradicts.
Hmm, let me re-verify: after selecting the dot at (1,1), I pressed RIGHT. Diff: only (0,2 W→w). So the dot didn't move. Then ACTION7: nothing. Then I clicked (1,3): merge happened.
So the mechanic might be: click dot A to select; the game highlights the cell where A would merge with an adjacent dot in some direction; click that highlighted cell to execute the merge.
But which direction? (1,1) was selected, and the highlighted cell was (1,3) = the result of merging (1,1)+(1,2) to the right. Why right? Maybe the last arrow key pressed determines the direction! Before selecting, I pressed RIGHT (the first probe). Then I selected the dot. The highlight (1,3) corresponds to a RIGHT move. Then I pressed RIGHT again (no change), ACTION7 (no change), and clicked (1,3) → merge executed.
So the flow is: press an arrow key to set the direction (or the arrow key itself attempts a move but only previews?), click to confirm? That seems roundabout.
Alternative: the arrow key moves the selected dot one step in that direction, but only if the destination is empty... the destination (1,2) is occupied by a dot. In 2048, moving right with an adjacent same-value dot causes a merge. Maybe the game shows a preview (g tile) of the merge result, and you have to click to confirm?
Let me test more cleanly. Current dots: (1,3), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5). Let me select the dot at (1,3) and see which cell gets highlighted. If the mechanic is "the last arrow key direction is still RIGHT," then selecting (1,3) should highlight (1,5)? Because (1,3)+(1,4) merge to the right → (1,5). Let me test.
